style: An oil painting in the manner of nineteenth-century academic history painting: rich palette, dramatic chiaroscuro, visible brushwork, painterly and cinematic, 16:9. England and France in 1775: tricorn hats, greatcoats, knee-breeches, buckled shoes, candle and lantern light, no modern objects. No captions, no signature, no frames, no black bars or borders.

people.lorry: Mr. Jarvis Lorry: a neat, orderly English banker of about sixty, clean-shaven, a small sleek crisp flaxen wig close to his head, a well-worn brown suit and waistcoat, brown stockings, plain buckled shoes, white linen
people.lucie: Lucie Manette: a young lady of seventeen, short, slight and pretty, with a quantity of golden hair and blue eyes, a smooth young forehead that lifts in an intent, inquiring expression
people.pross: Miss Pross: a tall, strong, red-faced Englishwoman with red hair, in an odd tight-fitting dress and an enormous tall bonnet
people.defarge: Ernest Defarge: a bull-necked, martial-looking Frenchman of thirty with crisply curling short dark hair, shirtsleeves rolled to the elbow, bare brown arms, good bold eyes
people.madame: Madame Defarge: a stout Frenchwoman of thirty, steady face, strong features, darkly defined eyebrows, watchful eye, a large hand heavily ringed, wrapped in fur with a bright shawl about her head, large earrings, knitting

beats.text: Dover, a bright cold November forenoon, 1775: the little narrow crooked town tucked under the white chalk cliffs, the grey-green sea breaking on the shingle beach, fishing boats drawn up; the elderly gentleman walks alone on the beach in his brown coat, the sea wind in his face. Luminous daylight, open sky, wide view.

Paris, a narrow cold grey street in the poor quarter of Saint Antoine, 1775: a great wine cask has fallen from a cart and burst on the cobbles; ragged men, women and children in wooden shoes and rags kneel and crowd to scoop the red wine from the stones with their hands, with broken pottery, with handkerchiefs; red wine stains the stones, the hands, the faces. Tall dark leaning houses, washing hung across, a grey sky.

A narrow grey Paris street in 1775: a tall gaunt man in a long ragged nightcap, his mouth stained red with spilled wine, reaches up and writes the word BLOOD on a pale stone wall in red wine with his fingertip; ragged men and women behind him gather spilled wine from the cobbles around a broken cask. The word BLOOD legible on the wall in wine-red letters. A grim, quiet moment.

Inside a dark low Paris wine-shop on a bitter day: behind the counter sits a stout, composed woman wrapped in fur, a bright shawl twined about her head, large earrings, her knitting laid before her; her husband, a bull-necked dark man in shirtsleeves with his coat slung over his shoulder, has just come in from the street; three rough customers at a table with wine cups glance up. Smoky, shadowy, a little grey daylight from the door.

A bare, dim garret under the roof, lit only by a narrow shaft of light from a half-opened door; a gaunt old man with a ragged white beard, a hollow face and wild white hair sits stooped on a low bench making a shoe, scraps of leather around him; the wine-shop keeper stands at the door, looking in. Very dark, one hard beam of light, dust in the air.

In a dim bare garret, the young woman with long golden curls sits on the low shoemaker's bench beside the gaunt white-haired old man; he has laid down his knife and, wondering, lifts a lock of her golden hair in his trembling hand to look at it; tears in her eyes; a single shaft of light falls on the two of them. Tender, hushed.
